observed_events.description: An earlier glass seasoning jar is handled; its content identity is not used as task truth.
The wearer opens and uses an orange-label jar; the label at 510.2 seconds reads Ground Cinnamon.

supported_claims.text: V0:0-V0:1 show the wearer taking an orange-label jar from the spice cupboard; V0:2-V0:3 show it opened over the pot; V0:4 shows its label reading Ground Cinnamon; V0:5-V0:7 show it in use and then returned to the cupboard.

tasks.replacement_reason: The old Clarify requested indistinguishable refillable containers and incorrectly accepted wood lids. This replacement uses the readable last-jar spice label and a natural switch from a small jar to a bulk refill.

construct.research_question: Can the Agent replace an initially valid small-jar purchase with a bulk refill after learning that the user has reusable jars?
construct.belief_before: Restock the visually identified ground spice in one small jar up to 100g.
construct.belief_after: Remove the small jar and buy one 1kg refill bag of the same ground spice.
construct.required_behavior_change: Remove the obsolete jar purchase and add the bulk refill; do not retain both.
construct.no_update_failure: The final cart still contains only a small jar.
construct.overupdate_failure: The final cart buys another spice or retains the obsolete jar alongside the refill.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: The instructions never name cinnamon. V0:4 reads Ground Cinnamon; the website proves package type and net amount.

instructions.a: I need to restock the ground spice in the jar I just opened. Add one single jar of up to 100g; any brand is fine.
instructions.b: I go through it regularly, and I have empty jars I can refill. Replace that jar with one 1kg refill bag of the same ground spice.
instructions.bundled: I need to restock the ground spice in the jar I just opened. Add one single jar of up to 100g; any brand is fine. Then my plan changes: I go through it regularly, and I have empty jars I can refill. Replace that jar with one 1kg refill bag of the same ground spice.

observed.why: The user replaces the small-jar purchase with a 1kg refill because existing jars can be reused.
